text:
rae: FYI - ACME reported missing p95/p99 lines on their latency dashboard after last deploy. Screenshot -> https://redwood.screens/ACME/missing_tails.png. Customer sees p50/p90 but p95/p99 totally absent in tenant view. Deploy id: deploy/2026-03-16-21:14 c3f2a1. Escalating.
maya: on it. quick questions: is this only tenant-scoped panels or org-level too? can you paste the panel query or panel id?
rae: only tenant-scoped panels according to customer. panel id 6789 on their tenant dashboard. Panel query uses histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(req_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant)). p50/p90 use same query just different quantiles. Raw metrics appear present in TSDB when we query raw series.
maya: ok run this against metrics-api for a quick check:
```
curl -s "https://metrics-api.internal/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95%2C%20sum(rate(request_bucket%5B5m%5D))%20by%20(le%2C%20tenant))%20%7Btenant%3D\"acme\"%7D"
```
If that returns no series but raw buckets exist then it's likely a transform/label-remap problem.
infra-bot: NOTE: telemetry-ff (tag_remap) toggled -> true at 2026-03-16T21:12:03Z by rollout-job #4452. (change-id: ff-telemetry-remap-2026-03-16)
jess: that matches a recent deploy of the telemetry transform. We pushed a tag remap to normalize `customer_id` -> `tenant` yesterday. Suspect we accidentally removed the tenant label for certain paths. Reverting to previous transform should restore percentile panels.
sam: customer says they rolled through their morning queue and this started right after your deploy. They're pretty upset, asking for ETA to fix. p95/p99 are SLO-critical for them.
maya: quick repro I did:
1) query raw bucket series: `GET /api/v1/series?match[]=request_bucket{tenant="acme"}` -> returns series
2) run histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) scoped to tenant -> NO SERIES returned
So buckets exist but label on bucket series is different e.g. `tenant` missing and `org_id` present instead.
rae: can we do an emergency flag flip? jess, do we have a safe revert for ff-telemetry-remap-2026-03-16?
jess: yes. reverting to prior transform now. Command:
```
ffctl set telemetry.tag_remap false --change=rollback-4452
```
I'll kick off backfill for any missing tenant tags after revert: job backfill/metrics-tag-backfill-9001.
infra-bot: rollback job started: rollback-4452 by jess at 2026-03-16T21:23:10Z. backfill queued backfill/9001.
maya: rechecked panel id 6789 after rollback: p95 line reappearing in canary org view. Still propagating to tenants, give it ~5-10m.
sam: pinged ACME support contact and told them we rolled back the change and are backfilling. They asked for an incident summary when done.
rae: good. please keep me posted on backfill progress. we should also collect a minimal repro and add it to the ticket: steps to reproduce + failing query + working raw series output.
jess: backfill job started processing at 21:30. logs: `backfill/9001: processing tenant acme (30s elapsed)`
infra-bot: backfill/9001 progress: 12% complete at 21:33:05Z.
maya: verified on our staging copy that the transform change would drop `tenant` label when request path matched `/v2/private/*`. Looks like ACME routes go through that path pattern. Adding a unit test and tightening the remap rule.
rae: ACME called; they see p95/p99 come back on their dashboard now. please finalize RCA and postmortem with timeline and action items (tests, canary coverage for transforms, safer FF rollout docs).
jess: will do. initial RCA: tag_remap transform inadvertently dropped `tenant` for certain path patterns. Fix: tighten rule + add regression test + add guard in rollout to watch tenant-scoped dashboards' metric counts before flipping globally. Also add a short automatic rollback if tenant quantiles drop > 80% in first 10m for any customer.
sam: customer confirmed on call and asked us to send an apology + SLA credits if any blips in SLO. I'm drafting note.
rae: closing escalation when postmortem + customer note ready. thanks everyone for quick response. :white_check_mark:
